claims.claim: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005); Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289; images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/
claims.note: Holds on every chronology in the cited sources. Birth 69 BC (Rosso: 'Cleopatra VII was born at 69 BC'); landing July 20, 1969 (NASA KSC-as11-40-5877: 'Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon July 20, 1969'), so 2,037 years forward. Back to the pyramid: Khufu's reign ends (Djedefra accession) at medians 2565-2603 BCE in Erdil S2 Table, giving 2,496-2,534 years; even Spence's low dates quoted by Sheisha (Khufu accession '2480 ± 5 BCE', Khafre '2448 ± 5 BCE') give about 2,380. Also holds from her death in 30 BC (1,998 forward against >2,400 back), so 'lived' is true across her whole life.

claims.claim: Hook as heard and seen at second two: 'Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing' (caption page 1 breaks after 'landing'); Look 1 shows the title card CLEOPATRA / QUEEN OF EGYPT · 69-30 BC; Look 2 has cut from the Waterhouse painting to Aldrin on the Moon with 'MOON LANDING' (~1.57 s).
claims.source_checked: src/generated/cleopatra-timeline.alignment.json ('landing' ends 2.322 s, 'than' starts 2.322 s); src/shorts/cleopatra*/index.tsx
claims.note: A viewer who leaves at 2 s takes away only that Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to something, with her dates 69-30 BC on screen. Nothing false is implied, and the full hook is itself true (claim 1). The popular form of this fact is the true one, so no correction is needed.

claims.claim: The pyramid was finished around twenty-six hundred BC.
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)
claims.note: Sheisha: 'the Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu Pyramid)'; the Journal of Merer, from 'a Khufu-age port', 'describes the transport of limestone ... to the construction site of the Great Pyramid of Khufu', so it was being built in Khufu's reign. Erdil S2 Table: Djedefra (end of Khufu's reign) medians 2565, 2577, 2586, 2603, 2603 BCE across models P1-P5; Khufu accession medians 2589-2632. Any completion date in or near his reign rounds to 'around 2600 BC'. The sources disagree (Sheisha also quotes von Beckerath 2554 and Spence 2480 ± 5 for Khufu's accession), but Erdil says the Low chronology 'is ruled out at 95% probability' for the Old Kingdom, and Sheisha calls the 14C chronology 'preferable as less subject to interpretation'. The SOURCES entry records the disagreement, as A3 asks. Caveat: no cited source gives a completion year; 'around' carries that.

claims.claim: Cleopatra was born in sixty-nine BC.
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289
claims.note: Rosso: 'Cleopatra VII was born at 69 BC from an illegitimate union of Ptolemy XII'.

claims.claim: Two and a half thousand years later.
claims.source_checked: Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005); arithmetic
claims.note: 2600 BC to 69 BC is 2,531 years (astronomical -2599 to -68). On Erdil's Djedefra medians (2565-2603 BCE) it is 2,496-2,534. 'Two and a half thousand' fits both.

claims.claim: From her to Apollo eleven is only two thousand.
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289; images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/
claims.note: 69 BC to AD 1969 is 2,037 years (no year zero); from her death in 30 BC ('The queen committed suicide in August 30 BC', Rosso) it is 1,998. NASA AS11-40-5903 is dated '(20 July 1969)', and KSC-as11-40-5877 says 'landed on the Moon July 20, 1969'. 'Only two thousand' is a fair rounding.

claims.claim: To Cleopatra, the pyramids were already ancient history.
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)
claims.note: Interpretive framing that rests on dates. Even the youngest Giza pyramid (Menkaure: Sheisha gives accession '2564 to 2524 BCE (1σ)', '2532 BCE (2)', down to '2415 ± 10 BCE (42)') was begun some 2,350 years or more before her birth. 'Ancient history' is fair for anything that old.

claims.claim: CLEOPATRA / QUEEN OF EGYPT · 69–30 BC
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289
claims.note: Rosso: 'as the last queen of Egypt'; 'born at 69 BC'; 'The queen committed suicide in August 30 BC'.

claims.claim: c. 2600 BC (pill under the pyramid; card 4 after 'FINISHED!'; both timelines)
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)
claims.note: Same basis as claim 3. It carries 'c.', and the spoken line has 'around'.

claims.claim: 69 BC (pill under Cleopatra; card 5; timelines)
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289

claims.claim: AD 1969 (pill under the Moon; timeline card)
claims.source_checked: images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/
claims.note: KSC-as11-40-5877: 'landed on the Moon July 20, 1969'; ksc-69pc-442: lift-off 'July 16, 1969'.

claims.claim: 2,531 / YEARS, ROUGHLY (pyramid to her birth)
claims.source_checked: Code: YEAR = {pyramid: -2599, cleopatra: -68, apollo: 1969}; BACK = -68 - (-2599); Erdil S2 Table
claims.note: 2,531 is exact arithmetic from c. 2600 BC to 69 BC, and the 'ROUGHLY' tag carries the uncertainty of the pyramid date (Erdil medians give 2,496-2,534). The count animates up to 2,531.

claims.claim: 2,037 / YEARS (her birth to Apollo 11)
claims.source_checked: Code: FORWARD = 1969 - (-68); Rosso; NASA records
claims.note: 68 + 1,969 = 2,037 years; both end dates are confirmed (claims 4 and 6).

claims.claim: CLOSER TO APOLLO BY ABOUT 500 YEARS (Look 1) / ABOUT 500 YEARS CLOSER (Look 2)
claims.source_checked: Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005); Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; arithmetic
claims.note: 2,531 - 2,037 = 494. On Erdil's five Djedefra medians the margin is 459-497, so 'about 500' holds on the radiocarbon chronology that Erdil (2025) and Sheisha both prefer. Note: on historical chronologies quoted by Sheisha the margin is smaller (Shaw, Khafre at 2558: ~452; von Beckerath, 2522: ~416; Spence, 2448: ~342). Erdil rules the Low chronology out at 95%, so the label stands. If the owner wants it robust to every chronology, 'BY CENTURIES' would be.

claims.claim: Timelines drawn in proportion to the years (Look 1 markers; Look 2 cards 6 and 8 cutouts and arcs)
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/cleopatra-timeline/index.tsx lines 55-68; src/shorts/cleopatra-cutout/index.tsx Timeline
claims.note: Positions are computed as x0 + (x1 - x0) * SHARE, with SHARE = 2531/4568 = 0.554. In Look 2 the arcs run from x0 to xc-18 and from xc+18 to x1, a ratio of about 1.26 against the true 1.24; the cutout pictures are offset by a few px for layout. Proportional, as shown.

claims.claim: Illustrated Cleopatra figure (channel gown, gold diadem), flat-shape Great Pyramid, a Moon with a flag, Giza at dusk
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/cleopatra-timeline/cast.ts, set.tsx, index.tsx
claims.note: A framing label, not a likeness claim: an obviously cartoon figure in the channel's house style (cast.ts: 'The silhouette is the channel's gown rather than Ptolemaic dress'). The Moon flag stands for 1969 and makes no factual claim.

claims.claim: Card 1: Waterhouse 'Cleopatra' painting, 'CLEOPATRA', credit 'A LATER PAINTING · IMAGINED'
claims.source_checked: Looked at public/cutout/cleopatra/cleopatra.jpg
claims.note: The credit claims only what the picture plainly shows: a 19th-century oil, signed 'J.W. Waterhouse' lower right, made long after its subject and imagined. Confirmed by looking at the image file. Its 1888 date is not shown on screen, so it is not checked.

claims.claim: Card 2: 'MOON LANDING' over Aldrin on the Moon (AS11-40-5903) with a bootprint (AS11-40-5877)
claims.source_checked: images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/
claims.note: NASA: AS11-40-5903 '(20 July 1969) --- Astronaut Edwin E. Aldrin Jr. ... walks on the surface of the moon ... during the Apollo 11 extravehicular activity'. AS11-40-5877: 'A close-up view of an astronaut's bootprint in the lunar soil ... during the Apollo 11 extravehicular activity'. The local files match the NASA renditions: the bootprint correlates at 0.99; aldrin.jpg is the same frame recropped, checked by eye. The screen does not say whose bootprint it is.

claims.claim: Card 3: 'GIZA PYRAMIDS' over the Roberts/Haghe lithograph 'Pyramids of Geezeh'
claims.source_checked: Looked at public/cutout/cleopatra/geezeh.jpg
claims.note: The label claims only that these are the Giza pyramids. The print plainly shows two large pyramids with the Sphinx's head to the right, which is Giza. Confirmed by looking. No date or credit is shown, so none is checked.

claims.claim: Card 4: Frith photograph, pyramid cut out, 'FINISHED!' then 'c. 2600 BC', credit 'AS PHOTOGRAPHED BY FRITH, 1858'
claims.source_checked: collectionapi.metmuseum.org object 286141 (accession 2005.100.555) and its image DP132062, compared with public/cutout/cleopatra/frith.jpg
claims.note: Met 286141: 'The Great Pyramid and The Great Sphinx', Francis Frith, objectDate 1858. The print is also signed 'Frith 1858' lower left, and the local file matches the Met image (correlation 1.0). Because the Met title names it the Great Pyramid, the cut-out pyramid labelled c. 2600 BC is Khufu's. The credit tells the viewer the stripped, weathered state is how it looked in 1858.

claims.claim: Card 5: Alma-Tadema painting, 'BORN' then '69 BC', credit 'A LATER PAINTING · IMAGINED, 41 BC'
claims.source_checked: Looked at public/cutout/cleopatra/second.jpg; Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289; Met API search (no record); christies.com.cn (not reachable); web search hits were only aggregators and Commons mirrors
claims.note: 'A LATER PAINTING · IMAGINED' is plain from the image. But '41 BC' says the picture shows the meeting at Tarsus, and that comes only from the painting's title, which no A2 source I could reach states: it is in a private collection, Commons and the aggregators don't count, and the Christie's lot page was not reachable. Rosso confirms the meeting itself ('In 41, the meeting of Antony and Cleopatra ... in Tarsus'), but Rosso's Fig. 21 is a coin, not this painting. Change: drop ', 41 BC' (credit 'A LATER PAINTING · IMAGINED'), or cite a catalogue raisonné or museum/auction record that gives the painting's title or subject.

claims.claim: Card 7: 'APOLLO 11' over the launch (KSC-69PC-442) and Aldrin beside the flag (AS11-40-5874)
claims.source_checked: images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/
claims.note: ksc-69pc-442: 'The Apollo 11 Saturn V space vehicle lifted off ... at 9:32 a.m. EDT July 16, 1969'. as11-40-5874: '(20 July 1969) --- Astronaut Edwin E. Aldrin Jr. ... poses ... beside the deployed United States flag during Apollo 11 extravehicular activity'. The local files match the NASA renditions (correlation 1.0 and 0.99).

claims.claim: Card 8: Roberts/Haghe 'Great Sphinx, Pyramids of Gizeh' lithograph with the Waterhouse Cleopatra pasted in, 'THE PYRAMIDS?', credit 'AN 1840s PRINT · COLLAGE'
claims.source_checked: Looked at public/cutout/cleopatra/sphinx.jpg at full size, cropped and enhanced; Met 591848 (Roberts/Haghe, 'The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt & Nubia', 1842-49); Cleveland Museum of Art record 1953.503 (openaccess-api.clevelandart.org and www.clevelandart.org not reachable); Commons full-size file (HTTP 429)
claims.note: 'COLLAGE' is plain from the image. 'PRINT' is plain too, with Roberts's pencilled title and a 'London Published by F.G. Moon ...' line. But the year in that publisher line cannot be read at 1280 px. The only legible date is the drawing inscription 'July 17th 1839', and public/SOURCES.json itself calls the lithograph '1839'. The Met dates the Roberts/Haghe publication 1842-49, but I could not tie this plate to it from an A2 record. Change: either give the credit as something the image proves ('A 19th-CENTURY PRINT · COLLAGE'), or confirm the plate's publication year from the Cleveland record 1953.503 or the full-resolution publisher line, and fix SOURCES.json's '1839' to match.

claims.claim: Card 9: Frith photograph toned sepia with a drawn cobweb, 'ANCIENT HISTORY', credit 'FRITH, 1858'
claims.source_checked: collectionapi.metmuseum.org object 286141 (accession 2005.100.555) and its image DP132062, compared with public/cutout/cleopatra/frith.jpg
claims.note: Met 286141: Francis Frith, 1858. The sepia tone and cobweb are plainly decorative. The framing label rests on claim 7.

claims.claim: Title: 'Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid'
claims.source_checked: As claim 1
claims.note: Same as the hook; holds on every chronology quoted in the sources.

claims.claim: Caption: 'The Great Pyramid was about 2,500 years old when Cleopatra was born. Apollo 11 came 2,000 years after her.'
claims.source_checked: Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005); Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289; images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/
claims.note: 2,531 years (2,496-2,534 on Erdil's medians), so about 2,500. 2,037 years from her birth and 1,998 from her death, so about 2,000.

claims.claim: Description: 'The Great Pyramid of Giza was finished around 2600 BC, by the end of Khufu's reign.'
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)
claims.note: 'Around 2600 BC' is supported (claim 3). 'By the end of Khufu's reign' is a further, specific claim that no cited source makes. Sheisha only places the construction site in Khufu's time (Journal of Merer), and the SOURCES block itself says 'No source states a completion year'. Change: 'The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for Khufu, whose reign ended around 2600 BC.' Or cite a source that says it was completed within his reign.

claims.claim: Description: 'Cleopatra VII was born in 69 BC, about 2,500 years later. From her birth to the Apollo 11 landing in 1969 is 2,037 years.'
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289; images-api.nasa.gov records as11-40-5903, as11-40-5877, as11-40-5874, ksc-69pc-442, KSC-as11-40-5877; images-assets.nasa.gov medium renditions compared with the files in public/cutout/cleopatra/; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)
claims.note: Same as claims 4-6 and 13.

claims.claim: Description: 'Published dates for Khufu differ by more than a century; even the latest still puts the pyramid some 2,400 years before Cleopatra.'
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)
claims.note: Sheisha: Khufu's accession 'ranges from 2613 to 2577 BCE (1σ)' ... 'or 2480 ± 5 BCE', a spread of up to ~133 years. Erdil: 'Offsets between the two can be as great as a century'. The latest (Spence) puts Khufu at 2480 and Khafre at 2448, so the pyramid falls about 2,380-2,410 years before 69 BC: 'some 2,400'.

claims.claim: SOURCES: Sheisha gives Khufu accession 2613-2577 BCE (radiocarbon, 1 sigma), 2589 (Shaw 2000), 2554 (von Beckerath 1997), 2480 +/- 5 (Spence 2000); Khafre 2558 (Shaw) or 2586-2548 (radiocarbon); Menkaure 2564-2524 (radiocarbon) or 2532 (Shaw); Khafre 2448 on Spence

claims.note: Verbatim in the text: 'the accession date of Khufu (Fig. 4) ranges from 2613 to 2577 BCE (1σ) according to the 14C-based chronology (33) while other sources place the onset of his reign at 2589 BCE (2), 2554 BCE (41), or 2480 ± 5 BCE based on astronomical observations (42)'. Khafre: '2586 to 2548 BCE (1σ) (33) or ... 2558 BCE (2), 2522 BCE (41), or 2448 ± 5 BCE (42)'. Menkaure: '2564 to 2524 BCE (1σ) (33) with centers on 2532 BCE (2)'. Refs: 2 = Shaw, Oxford History of Ancient Egypt 2000; 33 = Bronk Ramsey et al. 2010; 41 = von Beckerath 1997; 42 = Spence, Nature 2000.

claims.claim: SOURCES: Sheisha calls it 'the Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu Pyramid)'; Journal of Merer records limestone taken 'to the construction site of the Great Pyramid of Khufu'

claims.note: Both phrases are verbatim in the Significance section and the introduction. The Merer quote is Sheisha's paraphrase of the papyrus, not the papyrus's own words, which is how the SOURCES entry attributes it.

claims.claim: SOURCES: Erdil 2025: 'Offsets between the two can be as great as a century'; S2 Table puts Djedefra's accession at a median of 2565-2603 BC across its five models
claims.source_checked: Erdil et al. 2025 PLOS ONE 20(5) e0314612 article XML (journals.plos.org) and S2 Table PDF (supplementary s005)

claims.claim: SOURCES: Rosso: 'Cleopatra VII was born at 69 BC'; 'The queen committed suicide in August 30 BC'; 'the last member of Ptolemaic Dynasty'; meeting with Antony at Tarsus in 41 BC

claims.claim: SOURCES 2: 'Cleopatra VII Philopator ... She was the last ruler of the Macedonian Greek Ptolemaic dynasty'
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021 Toxicology Reports 8:676-695 full text, Europe PMC PMC8042289
claims.note: Minor, SOURCES prose only, never shown to viewers. Rosso has 'last member of Ptolemaic Dynasty', 'the last queen of Egypt' and a 'Macedonian princess'. The epithet 'Philopator' does not appear for her in Rosso, and 'last ruler' is not Rosso's wording (Caesarion was nominally co-ruler). Change to Rosso's wording ('the last queen of Egypt, last member of the Macedonian Ptolemaic dynasty') or cite a source for 'Philopator'. The on-screen 'QUEEN OF EGYPT' is unaffected.

claims.claim: SOURCES 1/3/4/5: arithmetic: lowest chronology ~2,380 years older; Spence ~150 years younger; 2,496-2,534 on Erdil; 2,037 = 68 + 1,969; 1,998 from death; margin 494 (459-497); 2,570 against 1,998
claims.source_checked: Arithmetic on the confirmed dates

claims.claim: SOURCES 6: the Giza pyramids were built roughly 2,300 to 2,500 years before her birth; Meroe's pyramids are not the subject
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS full text, Europe PMC PMC9477388 (fullTextXML), doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119

claims.claim: SOURCES 7: Cleopatra stands 55.4% of the way from the pyramid to the Moon
claims.source_checked: Arithmetic; code SHARE
